items.title: Replacement for TableTools addon (Firefox)
items.summary: As described in my other question (see there for some background), I need replacements for some Firefox addons which should work with v57+ – i.e. they should be Web Extensions. In this case here, my question is about TableTools . Requirements: allows to sort a table by a column either numerical or alpha-numerical (must-have) filter tables by a column value (e.g. "Name" equals "Miller", "Age" is below 50, "City" contains "ton").

items.title: Regression testing tool?
items.summary: I'm starting a scientific computing, command line project using source code that has no automated testing. The previous developer compared results by hand. Before I make changes, I want to set up some testing. What I think would work best would be a regression testing tool. What I have in mind is a tool which: Is configured with a list of regular expressions representing lines to ignore. E.g., lines with absolute file paths, timing statements, output which includes system information (e.g. a user name, machine name), etc. Accepts a list of example command lines w/ input file(s).

items.title: MP3 Player Timestamp Tag/Marker
items.summary: I'm not really sure what to name this thing I'm looking for, but I've been recording my classes and playing them at home to study. It's hard to go back to topics, and most of my time is consumed just finding which timestamp/topic I'm looking for in one recording. (Mind you, these are multiple days/lessons so there's A LOT.) Maybe y'all know some app I can download where I can add tags/note on timestamps so I can just go back to them without any hassle. I'd really appreciate any suggestions or help I'll get here. TIA!!

items.title: How do I give my Hermes agents permanent memory, institutional knowledge, and intelligent model routing?
items.summary: I fundamentally want two things from my Hermes agents: I want them to remember everything I ever tell them, and I want them to develop an institutional memory comparable to that of an actual organization. By persistent memory, I mean the ability to reliably recall previous conversations, decisions, preferences, instructions, and their underlying rationale, irrespective of how much time has elapsed, how many sessions have occurred, or which model is being used.

items.title: Software to normalize audio on the fly from Blue Yeti mic (for Windows)
items.summary: I have a Blue Yeti microphone. It stands on the table, so the volume depends on how close I am to the microphone. In addition, various programs (telegram, discord, viber etc..) have their own "improvements" for sound. Therefore, every time I learn from the interlocutor that I am heard either too loudly or too quietly. It's very tiring for me to have to adjust to each individual program every time. I am looking for a solution to this problem. It would be nice to have some program, that takes care of the audio processing before that audio gets into the messenger.

items.title: What is the best fitness app for logging calorie intake, log exercise details, create weekly workout plans?
items.summary: I'm looking for an android app that has below features: Calorie Counter(including macros) Log body size and weight measurements Create weekly/monthly workout plan day by day to ease remembering the exercises on the gym. I'm not an expert so most of the time I need to go to Youtube and check how was that exercise done. Track and log exercise details like repetition number, how much did I lift and how much did I struggle I tried most of the famous fitness apps but most of them are focusing on either diet or workout. I couldn't find one to track all of them in one app.

items.summary: I'm researching ways to manage large volumes of historical business data while keeping storage organized, secure, and accessible when needed. I'm interested in data archiving software that can help with long-term retention without requiring all archived information to remain on expensive, high-performance storage. My main requirements are: Scalability: The solution should accommodate growing volumes of files and records. Retention management: It should support configurable retention policies.

items.title: How to Transfer Photos from iCloud Photos to Google Drive
items.summary: I'm looking for a convenient way to transfer photos from iCloud Photos to Google Drive. I have photos stored in my Apple account and want to move a copy of them to Google Drive so I can access and manage them more easily across different devices. I've been exploring different options, including downloading photos from iCloud and uploading them manually, but that can become time-consuming when dealing with a large photo library. I also came across All Cloud Hub , a multi-cloud management platform available as a web app and mobile apps for iOS and Android.

items.title: Java library for parsing Javadoc comments
items.summary: I would like to be able to programmatically convert Javadoc comments (such as those in the generated code of LWJGL ) to other formats (such as Markdown ). This would allow me to do things like automatically generating an idiomatic Clojure wrapper for LWJGL with human-readable docstrings. I can pick the Javadoc comments out of a source file using JavaParser , but that's where I get stuck.

items.title: Do you know a free program that keeps track of available software updates?
items.summary: I need to keep track of several software applications on my computer in a local network. All my software updates are available within this (offline) network and I am looking for a tool, that keeps track of possible updates. The optimal way would be: The program checks every night for updates within local network and (if the corresponding program is not running), it installs those update. One important addition: I need to keep track of my own programs.

items.title: Firewall app for MacOS that I can quit
items.summary: I know there is a few firewall solutions for Mac, I use one - "Little Snitch" and while it's great, it does not satisfy one of my requirements. My use case is as follows: I'm offline, maybe even in airplane mode, no network connectivity whatsoever and I'm running Mac on battery and just want to maximize its run time. I would like to quit as many apps as possible. Little Snitch would not let me quit/exit the app when/if I do not need it at the time. The only solution to unload it from memory is to uninstall the app.

items.title: What software can help me organize and manage personal files stored across multiple cloud storage services?
items.summary: I'm looking for software that can help me manage personal files stored across multiple cloud storage services from one place. My main requirements are: Unified file management: Browse and organize files from different cloud storage accounts. Easy file access: Access documents, photos, and other personal files without repeatedly switching between services. File synchronization: Keep selected folders synchronized across devices. Security: Support secure account access and protect personal files. Backup support: Make it easier to maintain copies of important files.

items.title: Prioritise, categorise and share To Do list
items.summary: I'm looking for a way of creating a To Do list. There are 4 of us in my team and each person will have a list of tasks. I want to set a priority and category to each task and have each assigned to one of us. I'd like to be able to see all tasks in a single list and also be able to filter them by team member, priority and category. Ideally, I'd like to be able to add notes in an individual task. I could do it in Excel but wondered if there is any software that does it out of the box. Also, I work for the health service and paid software won't be an option unfortunately. Thanks.

items.title: Open-source Google Keep alternatives?
items.summary: Is there any comparable alternative to Google's Keep? Features I require: notes must support including images (via copy and paste) and other files (PDFs) and treat them as attachments/image gallery, not necessarily inline (because there may be many images/large images) notes, images and PDFs must be indexed/searchable (via OCR (ie easyocr)) I wrote a note taking app with integrated live search ( https://github.com/jjYBdx4IL/ajax-solnotes ), but abandoned it because Google Keep does perfect OCR on images, which I can just copy and paste into notes there.

What I see in my personal spending and habits: I get free tokens from my company, and I spent between 3k-5k a month at the start of the year. items.title: Are junior devs beyond screwed?
items.summary: I decided to finish my degree at the ripe age of 30 and I can't get an internship even though I attended a T25 school. I'm well away of power dynamics and nepotism and how the real world works, especially in the age of DEI and offshoring. I was banking on being able to at least partially overcome that but it seems as the the very existence of such an opportunity has been completely annihilated. If you're not prodigious, a nepo hire, or a startup founder it seems like you're perpetually taking it up the arse.

items.title: Everything will get breached. How do you limit the blast radius?
items.summary: Got another breach email this morning, this travel operator had my passport number and travel history stored. At this point I feel every service we use is going to get dumped eventually. I consider unique passwords and hardware 2FA as no brainers, they stop credential stuffing, but they don't help when a service leaks your actual identity. There are just so many services that require personal data like your passport number, phone number etc.

items.title: Why are so many services using email magic links for login?
items.summary: I've noticed a big uptick in login screens defaulting to sending email magic links rather than asking for a password. Notably Claude does this (which during the Outlook outage last week completely blocked me from accessing it). I can only assume that this is a misguided attempt to make login easier for the people who use the Forgot Password link all the the time instead of a proper password manager. It's 1FA where your single factor is access a different service (your email) rather than a known secret. Is there an actual best practice HIG or security guideline that recommends this approach?

items.title: Tool: Kiri
items.summary: Docker Desktop alternative. What we like: Single, Docker-compatible daemon (CLI, Compose, buildx). Performance optimized with a small memory footprint. Includes networks, volumes, k8s. Dev tools like auto-HTTPs endpoints with publicly sharable URLs. Supports macOS, Windows, Linux. What we dislike: Non-native UI, unlike something like Orbstack (which is macOS only). “Machines” are containers with filesystem access, not true VMs.

items.title: Tool: Jiff
items.summary: Datetime library for Rust. What we like: Understands timezones natively and handles daylight sayings. Built-in handling of common date operations like durations, differences, calculations, geo regions. Uses Rust-native formatting and display options, including friendly formats. What we dislike: Shows you how complex dates and times actually are, but that probably means fewer bugs!
